root_cause.text: In `decode_choice()` in `net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_h323_asn1.c`, the boundary check before `get_len()` uses the uninitialized variable `len` (which is 0), allowing an out-of-bounds read when the bitstream is exactly consumed.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "In decode_choice(), the boundary check before get_len() uses the variable `len`, which is still 0 from its initialization... When the bitstream is exactly consumed (bs->cur == bs->end), the check nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, 0, 0) evaluates to (bs->cur + 0 > bs->end), which is false. The subsequent get_len() call then dereferences *bs->cur++, reading 1 byte past the end of the buffer." The patch fixes this by changing `len` to `2` (the maximum bytes get_len() may read).

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure at least 2 bytes are available before reading the length field in H.323 choice decoding to prevent out-of-bounds access.
intent_record.what: Replaced the parameter `len` with literal `2` in the call to `nf_h323_error_boundary()` in the `decode_choice` function.
intent_record.how: Changes the boundary check from verifying that the bitstream has at least `len` bytes remaining to always requiring at least 2 bytes before calling `get_len()`.
